Privacy policy

Effective November 15, 2026.

This policy covers the StarPeople.ai website and StarPeople Publisher, the publishing tool operated by the UFO Files project to share news, field observations, and findings from public research records on our own social pages. It does not replace the policies of LinkedIn, GitHub, Internet Archive, OpenAI, Hush Line, or independent field-station operators.

Website visitors

This website does not require an account. We do not add advertising trackers or sell visitor information. Our hosting and delivery providers, including GitHub Pages, may process IP addresses, browser information, and request logs to deliver and secure the site. Images, videos, and links served by third parties, including Internet Archive, can disclose your IP address and browser request information to those services when loaded. Their own privacy policies apply.

LinkedIn authorization

StarPeople Publisher is an internal tool for our authorized page administrators. When connected to LinkedIn, it uses administrator-granted authorization to publish to the StarPeople AI organization page. It stores the organization identifier, granted permission scopes, token-expiration information, and the access credentials needed to make those requests. Credentials are kept in restricted local storage, separate from public source code and publishing evidence. They are not included in posts or sent to the AI editorial process.

The publisher is designed to create posts on our organization page. It does not collect LinkedIn private messages, connection lists, follower profiles, or member comments. It keeps publication identifiers and outcomes so it can avoid duplicate posts and diagnose delivery problems. LinkedIn separately processes account information and activity under its own Privacy Policy.

Sources and AI-assisted preparation

The publisher uses publicly available news and research sources, published machine-readable records, and field observations that have already been approved for public archiving. Drafts and supporting public evidence may be processed by OpenAI services to select material, prepare summaries, and check statements against sources. We do not intentionally send LinkedIn credentials, private correspondence, precise private station coordinates, or unpublished personal data into that editorial process.

Public records may contain personal information supplied by their original publishers. Public availability does not make that information appropriate for a social post. The publisher is instructed to omit identifying witness details and other sensitive personal information. Automated summaries can still contain errors. Contact us to report an inaccurate statement or a privacy concern.

Public posts and third parties

Published posts, citations, and linked evidence are public and may be copied or retained by other people or services. Removing a post from an account we control cannot guarantee removal of independent copies or the underlying source archive. We do not sell the information handled by the publisher or use it for advertising profiles.

Retention and security

Authorization credentials are retained while the publishing connection is active and usable. A page administrator can revoke the app's access through LinkedIn and ask us to remove locally stored authorization data. Drafts, source snapshots, and processing logs are retained for up to 90 days for troubleshooting. Minimal publication identifiers, content fingerprints, and duplicate-prevention records may be retained while the service operates. Public posts remain available until removed. We use restricted file permissions and separate credential storage; no system can guarantee absolute security.

Your requests

To request access to, correction of, or deletion of information we control, disconnect the publishing integration, or report a privacy issue, contact the UFO Files project through Hush Line. Include the relevant page, post, or source URL and the nature of your request. Please do not send passwords, access tokens, or government identification. We may need enough information to verify that a request concerns you or an account you administer. Requests about another service's account data or an original record should also be directed to that service or record custodian.

Changes

We will update this page and its effective date when the publisher's data practices change materially.
